question: In 1983 handwriting experts compared a Hitler diary page with known samples of his hand. Why did they wrongly confirm it?
options: Their reference samples were forged too
The forger had traced genuine letters
Hitler's hand varied too much to judge
answer: Their reference samples were forged too. Among the documents supplied as genuine Hitler writing was material from the same forger, Konrad Kujau. A match between two fakes by one hand proved only that one man wrote both. Stern had paid 9.3 million marks; within two weeks of publication, chemists found post-war whitener in the paper.
move: Two checks that drink from the same well are one check.
ask: Which two confirmations of mine are really one source asked twice?
trap: Tracing, the forger's familiar trick for copying a signature.
reference: Robert Harris, Selling Hitler: The Story of the Hitler Diaries, Faber and Faber, 1986
